title: HSC Assessment Profile
text:
Direct Assessment: Standalone equations (e.g., \(2 \cos^2 x + \sin x - 1 = 0\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\)), typically worth 2–3 marks.
Embedded Assessment: Crucial final step in complex calculus problems (finding stationary points).





Lost Solutions: Students algebraically divide by trig terms (e.g., \(\cos x\)), unwittingly discarding valid intersection points.
Quadrant Slips: Correct reference angle, but failure to apply ASTC rules across the restricted domain.

title: Welcome
text:
Welcome

Data-driven strategy: Targeting high-yield NSW Syllabus trigonometric concepts.
Focus on process over rote memory: Emphasising conceptual linkage to reduce cognitive load.
Ready-to-teach: Designed for direct classroom application and interactive learning.


The “Where” of Mathematics The Victorian Government states: “A domain name is a unique name that identifies your website’s location on the internet.”
Fill in the blanks by choosing the correct mathematical terms:

A domain is the set of [input / output] values that identifies where a function is defined.
The domain of a trigonometric function is the set of [angle / ratio] values for which the function is defined.
When solving trigonometric equations, the domain is the specific interval over which we identify our [solutions / amplitudes].

title: Examples
text:
// Master helper function for the interactive unit circle widget
function drawUnitCircle(angle_deg) {
  const rad = angle_deg * Math.PI / 180;
  const cos_v = Math.cos(rad).toFixed(2);
  const sin_v = Math.sin(rad).toFixed(2);
  const tan_v = Math.abs(Math.cos(rad)) < 0.001 ? "Undef" : Math.tan(rad).toFixed(2);
  
  return html`
    <div style="text-align: center; margin-top: 10px;">
      <svg width="240" height="240" viewBox="-1.5 -1.5 3 3" style="background:#fdfdfc; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:8px;">
        <!-- Axes -->
        <line x1="-1.4" y1="0" x2="1.4" y2="0" stroke="#ccc" stroke-width="0.02" />
        <line x1="0" y1="-1.4" x2="0" y2="1.4" stroke="#ccc" stroke-width="0.02" />
        <!-- Unit Circle -->
        <circle cx="0" cy="0" r="1" stroke="#005eb8" stroke-width="0.03" fill="none" />
        <!-- Angle Ray -->
        <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="${Math.cos(rad)}" y2="${-Math.sin(rad)}" stroke="#d55e00" stroke-width="0.05" />
        <circle cx="${Math.cos(rad)}" cy="${-Math.sin(rad)}" r="0.08" fill="#d55e00" />
      </svg>
      <div style="font-size:1rem; margin-top:10px; color: #2b2b2b;">
        <b>sin:</b> ${sin_v}  |  <b>cos:</b> ${cos_v}  |  <b>tan:</b> ${tan_v}
      </div>
    </div>
  `;
}








Solve \(\sin(2x) = \sin(x)\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\). (Double the angle, same value)






Step 1: Expand

\(2\sin(x)\cos(x) = \sin(x)\)



Step 2: Divide (Incorrect)

Divide both sides by \(\sin(x)\): \(2\cos(x) = 1\)



Step 3: Solve

\(\cos(x) = \frac{1}{2}\) \(\implies x = \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{5\pi}{3}\) (We lost the solutions where \(\sin(x) = 0\)!)







Step 1: Expand

\(2\sin(x)\cos(x) = \sin(x)\)



Step 2: Rearrange & Factorise

\(2\sin(x)\cos(x) - \sin(x) = 0\) \(\sin(x)(2\cos(x) - 1) = 0\)



Step 3: Solve

\(\sin(x) = 0 \implies x = 0, \pi, 2\pi\) \(\cos(x) = \frac{1}{2} \implies x = \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{5\pi}{3}\)




viewof a1 = Inputs.range([-360, 360], {value: 60, step: 1, label: "Angle x (°)"})
drawUnitCircle(a1)





















Solve \(\sin(2x) = 2\sin(x)\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\). (Double the angle, double the value)






Step 1: Expand

\(2\sin(x)\cos(x) = 2\sin(x)\)



Step 2: Divide (Incorrect)

Divide both sides by \(2\sin(x)\): \(\cos(x) = 1\)



Step 3: Solve

\(x = 0, 2\pi\) (Missed a valid intersection!)







Step 1: Expand

\(2\sin(x)\cos(x) = 2\sin(x)\)



Step 2: Rearrange & Factorise

\(2\sin(x)\cos(x) - 2\sin(x) = 0\) \(2\sin(x)(\cos(x) - 1) = 0\)



Step 3: Solve

\(\sin(x) = 0 \implies x = 0, \pi, 2\pi\) \(\cos(x) = 1 \implies x = 0, 2\pi\)




viewof a2 = Inputs.range([-360, 360], {value: 180, step: 1, label: "Angle x (°)"})
drawUnitCircle(a2)





















Solve \(\sin(2x) = \sin^2(x)\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\). (Double the angle, square the value)






Step 1: Expand

\(2\sin(x)\cos(x) = \sin^2(x)\)



Step 2: Divide (Incorrect)

Divide both sides by \(\sin(x)\): \(2\cos(x) = \sin(x)\)



Step 3: Solve

\(\frac{\sin(x)}{\cos(x)} = 2 \implies \tan(x) = 2\) \(x \approx 1.107, 4.249\) (Lost solutions again!)







Step 1: Expand

\(2\sin(x)\cos(x) = \sin^2(x)\)



Step 2: Rearrange & Factorise

\(2\sin(x)\cos(x) - \sin^2(x) = 0\) \(\sin(x)(2\cos(x) - \sin(x)) = 0\)



Step 3: Solve

\(\sin(x) = 0 \implies x = 0, \pi, 2\pi\) \(\tan(x) = 2 \implies x \approx 1.107, 4.249\)




viewof a3 = Inputs.range([-360, 360], {value: 63, step: 1, label: "Angle x (°)"})
drawUnitCircle(a3)





















Solve \(\sin(3x) = 3\sin(x)\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\). (Triple the angle, triple the value)






Step 1: Divide (Incorrect)

Divide both sides by \(\sin(x)\): \(\frac{\sin(3x)}{\sin(x)} = 3\)



Step 2: Bad Cancellation

Cancel the ‘sin’ terms: \(\frac{3x}{x} = 3 \implies 3 = 3\)



Step 3: Conclusion

“This is always true!” (Catastrophic failure of mathematical logic!)







Step 1: Apply Identity

\(3\sin(x) - 4\sin^3(x) = 3\sin(x)\)



Step 2: Rearrange

Subtract \(3\sin(x)\) from both sides: \(-4\sin^3(x) = 0\) \(\sin^3(x) = 0\)



Step 3: Solve

\(\sin(x) = 0\) \(\implies x = 0, \pi, 2\pi\)




viewof a4 = Inputs.range([-360, 360], {value: 0, step: 1, label: "Angle x (°)"})
drawUnitCircle(a4)

title: Pedagogical Rationale
text:
Dual Coding: Coupling abstract algebraic factorisation with visual geometry (unit circle) reduces cognitive load.
Productive Failure: The opening provocation induces a common error (dividing to lose a solution), priming students to accept the correct factorisation method.
Targeted Intervention: Directly mitigates the highest feedback-risk identified by HSC markers—domain errors and lost solutions.
